title: Payment Extension Terms on Residential Agreements Under Disconnection Notice — Customer Action Card
content:
# Payment Extension Terms on Residential Agreements Under Disconnection Notice — Customer Action Card

**Scope.** These terms set the Payment Extension — the one-time, single-installment kind of Payment Arrangement — enrolled on a residential service agreement of the customer whose status is disconnection notice pending. Extensions on other agreements follow the general Payment Arrangement terms, and the general eligibility, one-open-plan, lockout and single-installment rules are unchanged.

## Terms

1. The extension base must lie between the Payment Extension's smallest and largest eligible balance.
2. The amount carried by a payment extension is fixed only after every program bill of the customer that has been paid in full carries the forgiveness entry owed for it.
3. The amount carried by a payment extension is not worked out until every Winter Protection Plan of the customer that defaulted and has had its missed installments and good-faith payment paid inside its reinstatement window stands active again.

## The customer's acceptance — `accept_payment_extension_fc63ed0e`

**What the tool records.** The customer's own acceptance of a Payment Extension on one of their electric service agreements. The customer, acting in person, accepts a Payment Extension: the balance placed under it, the part of that balance to be paid now, and the amount carried to the extended date as one single installment. A new Payment Extension is created for the service agreement, set up by an agent, dated today, in pending down payment status with today as the last day for the payment due now, one installment equal to the amount extended, and nothing yet deferred off the agreement. A lookup of the customer's payment arrangements then shows the new extension.

**How it is invoked.** This is a customer's own tool. The agent unlocks it with `unlock_user_discoverable_tool` and hands it over; the customer themselves then runs it with `call_user_discoverable_tool`, naming `accept_payment_extension_fc63ed0e`.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `customer_id` | The customer reference number of the account holder, as returned by the customer profile lookup | Identifier |
| `service_account_id` | The service account number of the agreement the extension is for, as printed on the customer's disconnection notice and returned by the service agreement lookup | Identifier |
| `eligible_balance` | The balance placed under the extension | US dollars with 2 decimal places, a plain number such as 512.40 with no currency sign; stored rounded half-up to the cent |
| `down_payment_amount` | The part of that balance to be paid now | US dollars with 2 decimal places, 0.00 when nothing is due now; stored rounded half-up to the cent |
| `extended_amount` | The amount carried to the extended date as the single installment | US dollars with 2 decimal places; stored rounded half-up to the cent |

**Return.** A text receipt: "Payment Extension <arrangement_id> accepted on <service_account_id>: balance <eligible> USD, due now <due_now> USD by <YYYY-MM-DD>, extended <extended> USD." The reference number is that of the new arrangement, the date is today's date and the amounts carry 2 decimal places. Receiving this receipt means the extension is recorded.

## Illustration (hypothetical values)

The customer runs the tool with `customer_id` CUST-0005, `service_account_id` SA-0005, `eligible_balance` 512.40, `down_payment_amount` 0.00 and `extended_amount` 512.40 on a day dated 2026-04-14. The receipt reads: "Payment Extension <arrangement_id> accepted on SA-0005: balance 512.40 USD, due now 0.00 USD by 2026-04-14, extended 512.40 USD."
